correctness.rationale: On the Fourier representation of the claimed discrete Hardy boundary space, even and odd half-frequency exponentials are two orthonormal bases and their matrix elements are a unitary half-integer Cauchy kernel (sign conventions irrelevant to singular values). The exact frame operator is (I-P_J+U*P_LU)/2. Every maximal Cauchy minor is nonzero, so rank(C)=min(m,ell), and a finitely supported vector cannot have all of Ux supported on a finite L (rational function vanishing at infinitely many integers). Two-projection canonical angles then give 1/2(1±sqrt(1-sigma²)), essential 1/2 and unmatched 0/1 eigenvalues. For contiguous blocks the exact inverse of B_N=[1/(N+r-s+1/2)] has rank-one N^(2m-1) leading term and singular coefficient S_m, hence sigma_min~N^(-2m+1)/(pi S_m) and A~N^(-4m+2)/(4pi²S_m²). Independent high-precision m=1..3, N=40 normalized ratios 0.9876543,0.9635651,0.9397764 corroborate but do not prove the asymptotic. External source Proposition 7.2 could not be independently read in full; this is explicitly a dependency on a cited established Hardy model rather than self-contained proof of its equivalence.
